title: Join the checks
lesson: Parallel checks can share a frozen patch, but only fresh, acceptable results may cross the join into a separate human approval step.
limitations: Illustrative fixed workflow and timing; no measured speedup or quality guarantee.
PASS is a model review outcome, not proof of correctness; human evidence inspection remains necessary.
Failure blocks the approval-ready handoff, not engineers’ access to failing evidence; repair happens offscreen.
Read-only access and permission enforcement are configured outside the animation; persistent prompts cannot enforce permissions.
Audio was analysed but not physically listened to.
Original author self-review is preserved; subsequent comparative review and edits are credited separately.

transcript.text: A frozen patch A goes to two independent model reviewers: API compatibility and database migration. Both report a pass. The coordinator waits until both reports arrive, then sends a bundle to a human approver, who reviews and approves it.
A different patch B clears the earlier results and starts both checks again. The API report arrives first. The join shows one of two; approval waits while the database check continues.

The database reviewer reports a failure. Its red report reaches the join, blocking the approval-ready handoff. A red failure notice then reaches the human approver, whose state changes to REPAIR. Failing evidence is visible without permitting approval.

An engineer supplies a repaired patch C; the repair itself is offscreen. Both old reports are cleared because the code snapshot changed. Both checks run again, and their fresh passing reports reach the join.

The fresh bundle reaches the human approver for review and a separate approval decision. The result holds before fading to the opening background. This is an illustrative workflow, not a guarantee that passing model reviews establish correctness.

changes: Send a red failure notice to the human at 15.15s and show REPAIR at 15.95s while JOIN remains BLOCKED.
